title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of employers' organizations

description.narrative: India’s labour market is transforming under the pressures of technological disruption, global economic shifts, climate challenges, and regulatory reforms. The ILO’s CPO Strategy 2024-2025 aims to equip Employers' and Business Membership Organizations (EBMOs) to lead this transition towards a resilient, inclusive, and future-ready workforce. A key focus is digital transformation—enhancing member engagement, visibility, and service delivery through digital tools. Recognizing rapid shifts in the world of work, the strategy prioritizes capacity building to help EBMOs address future of work challenges and promote a Just Transition. The ILO will strengthen social dialogue to ensure employer, worker, and policymaker collaboration in shaping inclusive labour policies. EBMOs will be supported in adapting to evolving economic realities and engaging emerging sectors like platform work, electronics manufacturing, renewable energy, and the care economy. A key focus is responding to the needs of members and potential members in the changing world of work. India has been in the forefront of the digital transformation in the world of work. It has the largest amount of platform workers in the world. In this context EBMOs in India will be supported to expand their representativeness through membership engagement strategies on the platform economy. Collaboration with social partners, government bodies, UN agencies, development partners, DWT South Asia, ITC-Turin, and ILO Headquarters (ACTEMP) will ensure cohesive implementation. Through this strategy, the ILO reinforces its commitment to empowering EBMOs to navigate change and shape India’s future of work.
